To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the algebra G of diagrams, which is a combinatorial algebra, faithfully represents both H and U (LH), the algebraic structure of the creation– annihilation system, and that this algebraic structure is mirrored in the structure that G inherits from being a Hopf algebra.

the algebra H of creation and annihilation (or bosonic) operators of quantum theory has a combinatorial model in the form of a Hopf-algebra of diagrams, which we have denoted by G, and that the enveloping algebra U(LH) of the Heisenburg–Lie algebra LH has the same model.

1) The algebra of diagrams G is a Hopf algebra; 2) The Hopf algebra G faithfully represents the structure of U(H) and of U(LH) and thus of quantum mechanics and of the quantum theory of angular momentum; 3) The algebra G provides a combinatorial model for the creation–annihiliation system.

the combinatorial structure of the algebra of creation–annihilation operators and the associated Lie algebra, which are the fundamental objects in quantum theory.
the study of the algebra G and its relationship with H and U(L), which is the main subject of the present paper.
the study of the structure of the Heisenburg–Weyl and the enveloping algebras of the Heisenbug Lie algebra, as well as the structure of the algebra of diagrams G.

G is the combinatorial realization, the concrete model of quantum mechanics, and that H is the abstract model of quantum mechanics and that U(LH) is the abstract model for the algebraic structure of quantum mechanics.

we have found a combinatorial model that faithfully represents the algebraic structure of the creation and the annihilation operators of Quantum Mechanics.

the algebra G is the natural algebraic structure to use in a combinatorial description of second-quantized quantum theory.
